name: North Shore & Howe Sound
blurb: Vancouver's backyard. Resort-accessed snow on Seymour and Cypress in winter, and the rugged Howe Sound Crest Trail in summer. Low elevation means a short, wet ski season, and fog has caught out many parties close to the city.

name: Squamish
blurb: The granite capital of Canada. The Stawamus Chief, the Apron and the Smoke Bluffs are minutes from town, and the Sea to Sky Gondola puts Sky Pilot and Habrich within a day's reach. Tricouni sits to the north on the west side of the highway.

name: Tantalus Range
blurb: The skyline across the Squamish River. Steep granite, heavily glaciated and usually reached by helicopter from Squamish. A big-mountain playground for the traverse in summer and for steep skiing from the Haberl Hut in spring.

name: Garibaldi Park South
blurb: Diamond Head, the Garibaldi Neve and Garibaldi Lake. Volcanic peaks and big icefields reached by long approaches from Squamish and Rubble Creek. Classic day runs to the Black Tusk and Panorama Ridge in summer, glacier ski touring in spring.

name: Whistler & Spearhead
blurb: Lift access from Whistler Blackcomb puts you in glaciated alpine terrain within minutes: the Spearhead Range, the Musical Bumps and the Blackcomb and Decker glaciers. Wedge Mountain, the highest peak in Garibaldi Park, rises above the north end of the valley.

name: Pemberton
blurb: Mount Currie towers over the Pemberton valley with some of the biggest ski vertical in the corridor. Drier and colder than Whistler, with long spring days.

name: Duffey Lake Road
blurb: Road-accessed alpine on the edge of the interior. A drier, colder snowpack than the coast (forecast as a separate region), the Joffre Group's big north faces, and tree skiing straight from the highway.

name: Rogers Pass
blurb: Glacier National Park in the Selkirks, straddling the Trans-Canada Highway. Deep interior snow, steep treeline skiing and big glaciated tours, all managed through Parks Canada's winter permit system.

name: Canadian Rockies
blurb: Banff, Lake Louise, the Icefields Parkway and Jasper. Limestone peaks, big icefields and a cold continental snowpack: classic alpine rock and ice in summer, icefield traverses in spring.

name: Europe
blurb: The Alps: Chamonix, the Haute Route between Chamonix and Zermatt, and the Ortler in the Italian Alps. Hut-to-hut ski touring and classic alpine climbing with a European hut system behind you.

name: Japan
blurb: Hokkaido and the Japan Alps. Some of the most consistent cold powder anywhere, tree skiing on volcanoes and onsen at the end of the day.

name: Chile
blurb: The central and southern Andes: ski touring on volcanoes and big Andean peaks during our northern summer.
